extracted.intended_audience: newspaper editors, journalists, and politically engaged general readers
extracted.subtask_description: An early-20th-century personal/political essay offering norms and judgments about journalism, public leadership, and civic life; mixes memoir with prescriptive statements about conduct and public virtues. Useful as a source of ethical and practical criteria for journalists and political commentators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalistic ethics / rule of the press
rubrics_metrics.description: It has been my rule, aim and effort in my newspaper career to print nothing of a man which I would not say to his face; to print nothing of a man in malice; to look well and think twice before consigning a suspect to the ruin of printer's ink; to respect the old and defend the weak; and, lastly, at work and at play, daytime and nighttime, to be good to the girls and square with the boys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principles for responsible journalism: avoid personal malice, verify before destroying reputations, defend vulnerable people, treat colleagues and the public fairly. Anti-patterns: publishing malicious attacks, hasty consigning of suspects to 'printer's ink', failing to consider consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statesmanly steadiness and conviction
rubrics_metrics.description: The usual trend and phrase of his observations seem to be those of a special pleader, rather than those of a statesman...mark how often he has reversed himself to detect a certain mental and temperamental instability clearly indicating a lack of fixed or resolute intellectual purpose. This is characteristic of an excess in education; of the half baked mind overtrained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statesman should show consistency, firmness of intellectual purpose, and avoid the appearance of merely pleading a special cause. Anti-patterns: frequent reversals, doctrinaire affectation, overtrained but vacillating intellect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practicality in government (prefer facts, not theories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Government is a hard and fast and dry reality. At best statesmanship can only half do the things it would...I am a jingo myself. But a wicked material jingo, who wants facts, not theories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public policy and international schemes should be judged by practical effects and national interest rather than by abstract ideals or fanciful plans (example critique: League of Nations as a conceit that may 'bind the hands' of the nation). Anti-patterns: grandiose universal schemes that ignore pragmatic limits; sentimentalism over concrete policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities of great leadership (exemplified by Lincoln)
rubrics_metrics.description: His was the genius of common sense. Of perfect intellectual acuteness and aplomb, he knew all about the South, its institutions, its traditions and its peculiarities...He was a just man, abhorring proscription...not one vindictive, prescriptive word fell from his tongue or pen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure leaders by common sense, intellectual acuity, empathy for other regions/cultures, moral courage, inclination to conciliation rather than vindictiveness, and fidelity to constitutional limits. These are markers of moral and effective leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral requirement for writers ('pen with heart and brain')
rubrics_metrics.description: The pen is mightier than the sword only when it has behind it a heart as well as a brain. He who wields it must be brave, upright and steadfast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective, ethical writing requires both intellect and moral courage; writers should be upright and steadfast. Anti-patterns: rhetorical skill divorced from moral backbone; using the press for malice or opportunism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skepticism of mass will / mob fallibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The people en masse constitute what we call the mob. Mobs have rarely been right--never except when capably led.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caution against treating 'the people' as an infallible benchmark; recognize that mass opinion can be easily misled and dangerous without wise leadership. Anti-patterns: fetishizing 'the people' as a substitute for reasoned policy; pandering to mob impulses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics and dangers of fanaticism
rubrics_metrics.description: The fanatic is never either very discriminating or very particular. As a rule, for him any taking 'ism' will suffice. To-day, it happens to be 'whisky.' To-morrow it will be tobacco...Finally...it will become a misdemeanor for a man to kiss his wife.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fanaticism substitutes zeal for judgment and tends to sweep from one moral panic to another; evaluate reform movements for discrimination, proportionality, and respect for individual liberty. Anti-patterns: moral crusades that expand into intrusive policing of private life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tolerance and freedom of conscience
rubrics_metrics.description: Perfect freedom of conscience and thought has been my lifelong contention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates for unrestricted freedom of religious and political conscience; do not hate people for differences of opinion or worship. Practical application: preserve open pluralism in civic life and public discourse.
